'''Roy Walter Gould''' (April 25, 1927 – February 19, 2022) was an American electrical engineer and physicist who specialized in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]].<ref name="Cohen interview">{{cite web |last1=Cohen |first1=Shirley |title=Gould, Roy W. Interview by Shirley K. Cohen. Pasadena, California, March- April, 1996. Oral History Project, California Institute of Technology Archives |url=https://oralhistories.library.caltech.edu/109/1/OH_Gould_R.pdf |publisher=California Institute of Technology Archives}}</ref> In 1959, he (together with [[Alvin Trivelpiece]]) was the first to describe [[Electrostatic Wave|electrostatic waves]] that were propagating at the boundary of a magnetized plasma column, now commonly known as Trivelpiece–Gould modes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Trivelpiece|first1=A. W.|last2=Gould|first2=R. W.|date=1959|title=Space Charge Waves in Cylindrical Plasma Columns|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|language=en|volume=30|issue=11|pages=1784|doi=10.1063/1.1735056|s2cid=119373267 |issn=0021-8979|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/1676/1/TRIjap59.pdf}}</ref>

Gould was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1971 for pioneering contributions to microwave electronics and plasma physics and distinguished service in higher education.

== Early life and career ==
Gould was born in [[Los Angeles, California]] on April 25, 1927.<ref name="AIP bio">{{cite web |title=Roy W. Gould |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11512008.html |publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]] |accessdate=17 February 2020}}</ref> He studied at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] (bachelor's degree in electrical engineering in 1949), at [[Stanford University]] (master's degree in electrical engineering in 1950) and received his doctorate in physics from Caltech in 1956 (on microwave and radio noise from the sun).<ref name="Caltech bio">{{cite web |title=Emeriti Faculty: Roy W. Gould |url=http://www.aph.caltech.edu/people/rwgould |publisher=Caltech |accessdate=17 February 2020}}</ref> In 1951–52, he was a research engineer for rocket control at the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] of Caltech and from 1953 to 1955 at [[Hughes Aircraft Company|Hughes Aircraft]], where he researched electron tubes.

In 1955, he became an associate professor and 1960 professor of electrical engineering at Caltech. In 1974, he changed to the faculty of physics as professor of applied physics, and from 1980 he was Simon Ramo Professor. Since 1996 he was professor emeritus.

From 1979 to 1985, he was chairman of the division of engineering and applied science at Caltech. From 1970 to 1972, he was director of fusion research at the Atomic Energy Commission.

== Personal life ==
Gould died on February 19, 2022, at the age of 94.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pasadenanow.com/main/roy-w-gould-1927-2022 |title=Roy W. Gould (1927–2022) |author=Robert Perkins |work=Pasadena Now |date=2022-02-28 |access-date=2022-03-02}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1966, he became a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1966&unit_id=&institution=California+Institute+of+Technology|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2022-03-02}}</ref> He has been a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] since 1971<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nae.edu/29296/Dr-Roy-W-Gould|title=Dr. Roy W. Gould|website=NAE Website|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] since 1974.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/roy-w-gould-senzje/|title=Roy Gould|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> In 1994, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Gould&first_nm=Roy&year=1994|title=1994 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2022-03-02}}</ref>
